correctness.rationale: C PASS: Directly identify the published weighted L1 statistic with the full empirical/fitted Poisson mass-function L1 norm; Poisson Hellinger affinity removes estimated-mean noise with E|error|<=2/sqrt(n). Exact binomial absolute-deviation identity and bounded differences reduce the null limit to a Riemann integral. A uniform Poisson local central limit theorem and a Chebyshev tail cutoff give the critical n^2 scale; central-window L1 and overlap bounds prove the two endpoints. The Poisson modal mass has a strictly decreasing continuous envelope; its integer derivative jumps yield local 3/2-power singularities with an explicit nonzero coefficient. The included script actually passed 126 independent finite checks, which support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: O PASS, qualified: Full source sections defining the exact statistic and the original source conclusions were inspected. The 2023 thesis discusses fixed-parameter weighted tests and Poisson modes, not an increasing-intensity n-squared transition, Gaussian occupancy curve or its singularity ladder. The 2012 empirical L1 paper supplies concentration bounds; the 2009 occupancy paper supplies occupied-box approximations; neither inspected text states the exact combined theorem. Record-search comparisons produced related Poisson and multinomial results, but none covering this statistic-specific claim or implying its nonanalytic curve directly. A more general uninspected theorem might subsume a component.

value.rationale: V PASS: When the Poisson count distribution spreads across a number of cells of order sqrt(lambda), the fitted empirical-mass test changes sharply from a vanishing to a maximal null discrepancy as the cell count overtakes sample size. The exact profile permits quantitative calibration of the full null statistic in this otherwise unaddressed large-intensity setting. The countable modal-cusp ladder reveals concrete non-smooth parameter dependence that is not captured by generic consistency bounds; it is a structural property rather than a trivial tiny improvement.
